mission: Conjecture was founded in 2022 by EleutherAI veterans Connor Leahy, Sid Black and Gabriel Alfour. It argues that scaling ever-larger black-box models is dangerous and is building 'Cognitive Emulation' (CoEm): AI systems built from components that follow human-like, inspectable reasoning instead of one giant opaque model.

key_work.title: Cognitive Emulation: A Naive AI Safety Proposal
key_work.plain_summary: Proposes building AI that emulates human reasoning in bounded, understandable ways rather than training an all-powerful black box.

key_work.title: Multinational AGI Consortium (MAGIC): A Proposal for International Coordination on AI
key_work.plain_summary: Proposes a single international body with an exclusive mandate to develop the most advanced AI, plus a global halt elsewhere.

key_work.title: unRLHF: Efficiently undoing LLM safeguards
key_work.plain_summary: Showed that safety fine-tuning on open models can be removed cheaply.

key_work.title: Conjecture: A Roadmap for Cognitive Software and A Humanist Future of AI
key_work.plain_summary: The company's current plan for building controllable 'cognitive software'.

key_work.title: We Are Conjecture, A New Alignment Research Startup
key_work.plain_summary: Founding announcement explaining why the team left open-source model building to focus on alignment.

warnings.text: The AI industry is racing to scale ever-larger models without considering the risks.
Scaling makes it harder to notice when models are wrong and impossible to debug them.
AI's inner workings are uninterpretable, so its outputs are hard to trust.

recommendations.text: Build AI from understandable components that follow trusted human reasoning (Cognitive Emulation).
Coordinate internationally on AGI development (the MAGIC proposal).
Stop the race to ever-larger black-box models.
